description:
## Empirical anchor

2026-05-13 surfaced by PRINCIPAL during the substrate-architecture discussion as a sibling pattern to two-team-per-project. Multiple specialized teams coexist in the Stoa ecosystem; the substrate needs canon for how they interoperate.

Current state of the ecosystem (live):
- **the-stoa** — the forge; canonical substrate templates
- **ariadne-core-workspace** — Ariadne team (the first specialized derivative)
- **railway_stoa** — Railway team (in setup; will house Railway tooling agents + skills)
- **(future)** — additional teams (Conan team, factory-demo team, etc.)

Each team is itself a Stoa-substrate-deployed project. Cross-team work happens already (the ariadne team uses Railway; the railway_stoa team will produce skills the ariadne team consumes). But there's no substrate canon for how this works.

## The substrate-canon shape

Document the multi-team pattern in operating-disciplines.md:

- **Each team is its own project** with its own substrate (own bw, own deployed CAPTAINs, own memories). The Stoa team is the universal forge that produces deployable templates.
- **Cross-team interoperation happens via consumed artifacts**: skills, tooling, deployed services. The Railway team produces skills; the Ariadne team consumes them.
- **Cross-team bw coordination** uses the prefix-namespace convention (`stoa--`, `ariadne--`, `railway--`, etc.) + downward-only visibility rule (user-tier reads/writes down; project-tier never crosses to peer-project bw). Already partially canonized; this ticket makes it explicit for the multi-team case.
- **Cross-team requests** flow through user-tier POLYBIUS (the only seat with cross-tier visibility) OR through PRINCIPAL as broker. Project-tier teams don't directly dispatch into peer-project teams.
- **Naming + discovery** — how does a team know what other teams exist? Maybe a substrate-tier registry; maybe user-tier POLYBIUS knows; possibly just convention (peer projects in the user's `~/claude_projects/` directory).

## Substrate touch-points

- `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` — new section on multi-team architecture (cross-team interoperation conventions)
- `substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` — discipline for user-tier-POLYBIUS as cross-team broker
- Possibly: a substrate-tier registry convention (or skill) for team discovery

## Gauntlet

DAEDALUS + ADA + CATO. Substrate-prose edit. ~60-100 LOC.

## Sequencing

P2. Arc 25 candidate. Bundles naturally with two-team-pattern (same architecture-canon arc — two-team is intra-project; multi-team is inter-project).

## Cross-references

- Two-team-pattern ticket — sibling architectural canon (intra-project)
- Memory: `feedback_bw_visibility_is_downward_only.md` — partially canonizes cross-tier rules; this ticket extends to multi-team-explicit
- `substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/` — works across all consumer workspaces; this ticket frames it as multi-team-aware

## Empirical anchor for the cross-team pattern

The current bw → Ariadne integration is itself an example: bw (write substrate) + Ariadne (read projection) + hypergraph (relational extension). The "many projects from one substrate" finding (stoa--gq1) is the composability dimension; this ticket is the interoperation dimension.
title: Substrate canon: multi-team interoperation pattern (cross-team via bw substrate + consumed artifacts)
